chapter_title: A Tale of Three Intersecting Lines

detailed_sections.full_notes: When three lines intersect pairwise in a plane at three distinct points, they form a triangle. The three points of intersection are vertices, and the line segments connecting them are sides.

margin_notes.title: Direct vs Roundabout Path
margin_notes.content: The direct straight path between two points is always shorter than any roundabout path passing through a third point.

detailed_sections.full_notes:
Triangle Inequality Theorem: A triangle can exist if and only if the sum of the lengths of ANY two sides is strictly GREATER than the length of the third side.
Mathematical conditions for side lengths a, b, c:
1. a + b > c
2. b + c > a
3. c + a > b
Shortcut test: The sum of the two smaller side lengths must be strictly greater than the largest side length.

margin_notes.title: Quick Existence Check
margin_notes.content: Can sides be 3 cm, 3 cm, 7 cm? No, because 3 + 3 = 6 < 7.

detailed_sections.full_notes:
1. Equilateral Triangle: All three sides equal (a = b = c). An equilateral triangle of any positive side length always exists because a + a = 2a > a.
2. Isosceles Triangle: Two sides equal.
3. Scalene Triangle: All three sides unequal.

margin_notes.title: Equilateral Always Exists
margin_notes.content: For any side length s > 0, s + s = 2s > s is always true.

scripted_dialogues.speaker: Surveyor
scripted_dialogues.speech_text: Road distances are AB = 12 km, BC = 20 km, AC = 40 km. Can towns A, B, C form a triangle?

scripted_dialogues.speaker: Cartographer
scripted_dialogues.speech_text: No! AB + BC = 12 + 20 = 32 km < 40 km. It fails the Triangle Inequality Theorem!

scripted_dialogues.speaker: Teacher
scripted_dialogues.speech_text: The sum of the two smaller sides must strictly exceed the longest side.

stem_lab_drawers.title: Ruler & Compass Triangle Feasibility Tester
stem_lab_drawers.concept: Testing Triangle Inequality Theorem a + b > c
stem_lab_drawers.expected_outcome: Arcs fail to intersect (3+3=6 < 7), visually proving no triangle can exist.

formula_rule_engines.formula: a + b > c AND b + c > a AND c + a > b
formula_rule_engines.computed_expression: Boolean check if sum of smallest two sides > longest side
Third side c must lie strictly between difference and sum of other two sides
formula_rule_engines.example_demonstration: For sides 6 cm and 10 cm: |10 - 6| < c < 10 + 6  =>  4 cm < c < 16 cm

hotspots.title: Direct Path vs Detour
hotspots.popover_content: Direct straight path c is strictly shorter than detour path a + b (c < a + b => a + b > c).

hotspots.title: Triangle Inequality Theorem
hotspots.popover_content: Sum of any 2 sides > 3rd side (a+b>c, b+c>a, c+a>b). Test: Smallest two sum > longest side.

hotspots.title: Side-Based Classification
hotspots.popover_content: Equilateral (a=b=c, always valid for s>0), Isosceles (a=b!=c), Scalene (a!=b!=c).

hotspots.title: Compass Arc Construction
hotspots.popover_content: Compass arcs of radii a and b intersect to locate 3rd vertex iff a + b > c. Arcs fail if a + b <= c.
